title: Joining Ellington in 1926 and checking discographies
summary: Braud says he joined Ellington in 1926 and recorded until 1935; Allen quizzes him on Brunswick titles, and they agree the record books contain errors.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Yeah, well, you must have it by, that must be Bass Headwood. It might be. Yeah. It might be a couple times. How far back is it? I can tell you exactly. Well, I joined Dugaldon Band in 26. I made the records from 26 up until 35. Was it Dane at 26? No, I know it was in 26. From that until 35.

See, now he made East St. Louis Tudeloo and Birmingham Breakdown, Fort Brunswick, February 28, 1927. I remember that. That's why I can tell you. Yeah, that would be after you could join the band. Did you ever make New Orleans Lowdown and Song of the Cotton Feet? I remember them by that name.
I remember the, during the New Lowdown, but not the New Orleans Lowdown. Yeah. During the New Lowdown, that's a tune from Black Boy. Yeah, I remember that tune.
I've got a good record at home. I wish I had to hear them. Immigration Blues of the Creeper. Yeah.
Yeah. Did you make that record?
I made the Immigration Blues, but I don't remember the Creeper. Perhaps I did. Yeah.

Well, it's got this wonderful two-ball break line on one side. I can't remember which side. I think it's Immigration Blues. So, five stars. Oh, well, good. That settles a lot of stuff in my mind, you know. Yeah. And these books are not right. You've got to check them.
Well, sometimes they have them right, and sometimes they don't. Some things. It's like anything else. Everybody makes mistakes.
Yeah. That's what the guy said when he wrote the book. He says, this is not the Bible. Send me your correction. You know? Mm-hmm. And that's right. They need to check up on everything kept.
